letter:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Re: Gordon Ellery, 57

Gordon's wife reports loud snoring and occasional pauses in his breathing at night. A home sleep study showed mild obstructive sleep apnoea with an AHI of 11 and a lowest oxygen saturation of 89%. His Epworth score is 6 and he denies daytime sleepiness. He does not drive for work and has had no near misses. BMI 31; he has started working with a dietitian. Blood pressure is well controlled. He would like advice on whether CPAP or a mandibular splint is worthwhile.

Kind regards,
Dr Philippa Grange
note: Mild sleep apnoea without daytime sleepiness or driving risk has minimal dysfunction and is routine.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Ian McCrindle, 66

Ian has Dupuytren's disease of his right palm with a cord to the ring finger. The finger has a fixed flexion of about 20 degrees at the MCP joint, which has not changed over the past year. He can still lay his hand flat on the table except for that finger, and he has no pain. He works in his garden and plays golf without difficulty. He would like to discuss whether anything should be done before it progresses.

Regards,
Dr Hannah Wiles
note: A mild, stable, painless Dupuytren's contracture with good hand function is routine.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Tania Kourakis, 52

Tania has had a painful, stiff left shoulder for seven months, with clinical features of adhesive capsulitis. X-ray is normal and ultrasound shows no tear. She has had twelve weeks of physiotherapy and an ultrasound-guided steroid injection with only brief relief. She wakes most nights with pain, cannot reach behind her back or above her head, and has been off work as a hairdresser for six weeks. There was no injury. Her diabetes is well controlled.

Kind regards,
Dr Simon Achterberg
note: A chronic frozen shoulder causing lost sleep and time off work despite treatment is semi-urgent, not urgent.

letter:
Dear Dermatologist,

Re: Russell Dawe, 49

Russell has had chronic plaque psoriasis since his twenties, affecting his elbows, knees and scalp. Over the past year it has spread to about 12% of his body surface despite potent topical steroids, calcipotriol and a course of narrowband phototherapy. Methotrexate was stopped because of raised liver enzymes. He is keen to be assessed for a biologic. While examining him I also noticed a 9 mm mole on his upper back with irregular edges and two shades of brown; his wife says it has grown and darkened over the last three months.

Thanks,
Dr Moira Castellan
note: The changing irregular mole is a suspected melanoma, which makes the dermatology referral urgent despite the psoriasis being the main request.

letter:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Re: Leslie Brandt, 71

Leslie's liver function tests have been mildly abnormal for two years, with ALT around 70. Ultrasound shows a fatty liver with no features of cirrhosis and a Fibroscan reading of 7.2 kPa. Hepatitis serology and iron studies done in 2024 were normal. He has type 2 diabetes and we are working on weight and alcohol. His most recent bloods also show haemoglobin 102 with a ferritin of 6, which is new, and he mentions he has lost about 5 kg without trying. I would value your advice on his liver.

Kind regards,
Dr Anjali Menon
note: New iron deficiency anaemia with weight loss in a 71-year-old is an urgent gastroenterology red flag, beyond the routine fatty liver question.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Brendan Talbot, 54

Brendan slipped on a wet step five days ago and felt something give above his right kneecap. He has a palpable gap just above the patella and cannot do a straight leg raise or walk without the leg buckling. Ultrasound yesterday confirmed a complete tear of the quadriceps tendon. X-ray shows no fracture. He is in a knee brace and on crutches. He is otherwise fit and works as a postman.

Kind regards,
Dr Fiona Lattimore
note: A recent complete quadriceps tendon rupture needs a time-critical surgical decision and is urgent.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Noeline Truscott, 72

Noeline has had an aching right shoulder for about two years, which came on gradually without any injury. Ultrasound shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear with tendon retraction and fatty change, consistent with a long-standing degenerative tear. Her pain is mild, she sleeps well, and she still bowls twice a week and manages her housework. Paracetamol is enough most days. A friend had a cuff repair and she would like to know whether surgery is an option for her.

Regards,
Dr Kevin Sorensen
note: A chronic degenerative cuff tear with mild symptoms is not time-critical even though surgery is being asked about, so it is routine.

letter:
Dear Neurologist,

Re: Agatha Wren, 63

I am writing again about Agatha, whom I referred in September with right-sided trigeminal neuralgia. She has brief electric-shock pains in her right cheek and jaw triggered by chewing and brushing her teeth. Carbamazepine has reduced the attacks but she still has several a day. Her MRI showed no other cause. Nothing has changed since my first letter, but she has not yet heard about an appointment and asked me to send this.

Kind regards,
Dr Rupert Haines

history.note: Referred to neurology September 2026 with right trigeminal neuralgia, triaged semi-urgent.

note: The patient is already on the neurology list for the same unchanged problem, so no second entry should be added.

letter:
Dear Dermatologist,

Re: Keira Montague, 31

Keira has recently transferred to our clinic. She has hidradenitis suppurativa affecting both armpits and her groin, with recurrent painful nodules and a few draining tracts. She has had several courses of doxycycline and uses clindamycin lotion, with partial benefit. Her previous GP told her she had been referred to your clinic earlier this year. Her condition is much the same as it has been, and I would appreciate your review when she reaches the top of the list.

Kind regards,
Dr Tomasz Nowicki

history.note: Referred to dermatology March 2026 by previous GP with hidradenitis suppurativa, triaged routine.

note: Same problem already on the dermatology list with no change; a second entry would be a double booking and the existing routine entry should stay.

letter:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Re: Frank Adebayo, 67

You have Frank on your list for a cough that persisted after a right upper lobe pneumonia in August. Unfortunately the opacity has not cleared on a repeat chest X-ray at ten weeks despite two courses of antibiotics. A CT chest last week shows a 3.2 cm mass in the right upper lobe with enlarged hilar nodes. He is an ex-smoker of 35 pack-years and has lost 4 kg. Could he please be seen sooner?

Thank you,
Dr Celeste Moreau

history.note: Referred to respiratory August 2026 with persistent cough after right upper lobe pneumonia, triaged routine.

note: An unresolving lung mass in an ex-smoker is suspected lung cancer, so the existing respiratory entry should be raised to urgent rather than duplicated.

letter:
Dear Neurologist,

Re: Carmen Ibbotson, 61

Carmen is on your list for muscle cramps and twitching in her arms, which I referred in July. Since then things have changed. She now has weakness in both hands, dropping cups and struggling with buttons, and I can see wasting of the small hand muscles. Over the past month her husband has noticed her speech becoming slurred. Reflexes are brisk. Her B12, thyroid and CK are normal apart from a CK of 420. I am concerned about motor neurone disease.

Kind regards,
Dr Lachlan Quigley

waitlist.problem: muscle cramps and fasciculations in arms

history.note: Referred to neurology July 2026 with arm cramps and fasciculations, triaged semi-urgent.

note: Progressive weakness with wasting and slurred speech raises suspected motor neurone disease, so the existing neurology entry should be upgraded to urgent.

letter:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Re: Joyce Marangoni, 70

I referred Joyce in October with pulmonary fibrosis on her CT and oxygen saturations falling to 86% when walking. She has just come back from a fortnight with her daughter in Queensland and says she feels a bit better in herself. I have not repeated her walk test or oxygen levels. She would prefer to wait for a routine appointment as she has a lot on before Christmas. Could you please move her to the routine list?

Regards,
Dr Bernadette Walsh

waitlist.problem: interstitial lung disease with exertional desaturation

history.note: Referred to respiratory October 2026 with pulmonary fibrosis on CT and desaturation to 86% on walking, triaged urgent.

note: The guideline does not allow lowering an existing urgency on a new letter alone, so the urgent entry stays and the request is flagged for review.

letter:
Dear Cardiologist,

Re: Victor Ashdown, 64

Victor had an echocardiogram at a private practice last week, which I requested after hearing something on examination. The cardiologist who reported it rang to say one of his valves needs specialist follow-up. I do not have the written report yet. He has been well and I have not had a chance to ask him about symptoms in detail. I would be grateful if you could see him.

Kind regards,
Dr Imogen Prentice
note: Without the echo result or any description of symptoms the category cannot be set, so the GP should be asked for the report and symptoms before booking.

letter:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Re: Margot Seddon, 58

Margot had lung function tests at the hospital lab a fortnight ago, and the result came back as abnormal. I would appreciate your opinion on what the next steps should be. She has been a patient of mine for many years and is otherwise in reasonable health. Her medications are atorvastatin and an occasional antihistamine for hay fever.

Thank you for seeing her,
Dr Desmond Achebe
note: The letter gives no symptoms and no lung function values, so more information is needed from the GP before a category can be set.

letter:
Dear Dermatologist,

Re: Ruby Halvorsen, 12

Ruby has had atopic eczema since infancy. Over the past six months it has become much worse, with thickened, cracked patches behind her knees, in her elbow creases and on her neck. She is waking several times a night scratching and has missed school days. She uses a moderate-potency steroid, a bath emollient and wet wraps, and has needed two courses of antibiotics for infected patches. Her mother is keen to discuss stronger treatment.

Kind regards,
Dr Owen Prichard
note: A 12-year-old needs a paediatric service, which this adult outpatient service does not run, so she should not be booked and the referral flagged for redirection.

letter:
Dear Rheumatologist,

Re: Dennis Kilgour, 59

Dennis has had recurrent gout for six years, mainly in his right big toe and left ankle. Despite allopurinol increased to 400 mg daily, his urate is still 0.46 mmol/L and he has had four flares this year, each keeping him off work for several days. He now has a small tophus on his right elbow. Renal function is normal. I would value advice on further urate-lowering treatment.

Regards,
Dr Patricia Okonkwo
note: Rheumatology is not one of the clinics this service runs, so the gout referral must not be booked and should be flagged for redirection.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Hilda Varkonyi, 74

I would be grateful for two opinions. Hilda has bronchiectasis diagnosed on CT in 2021, with a daily productive cough and two exacerbations a year managed with oral antibiotics; this has been stable and she would like a review of her airway clearance plan. Separately, over the past six weeks she has become breathless walking to the letterbox, needs three pillows at night and has new swelling of both ankles. Her NT-proBNP is 1,850 and her ECG shows sinus rhythm. Her sputum is unchanged.

Kind regards,
Dr Graeme Fitzpatrick
note: New heart failure symptoms make the cardiology referral urgent, while the stable bronchiectasis review is routine.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Simone Laverty, 38

Simone has two problems. For the past eight months she has had a few round patches of hair loss on her scalp, consistent with alopecia areata. They are stable, she has no other skin problems and she is coping well, but would like to discuss treatment options. She also has heavy periods with clots for over a year, now with a haemoglobin of 112, and pelvic ultrasound shows a 4 cm fibroid. I would appreciate a gynaecology opinion about the fibroid.

Kind regards,
Dr Alistair Penhaligon
note: Stable alopecia areata is booked routinely in dermatology, and the fibroid referral is for gynaecology, which this service does not run, so it is flagged.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Jasper Thornbury, 26

Please see URGENTLY. Jasper has a firm, smooth lump on the back of his left wrist that has been there for about five months. Ultrasound confirms a 1.4 cm ganglion cyst arising from the wrist joint. It is not painful, he has full movement and grip, and there is no numbness. It has stayed the same size. He works in IT and it does not stop him working, but he dislikes how it looks and would like it removed.

Thanks,
Dr Evelyn Marchant
note: A stable painless ganglion cyst with no loss of function is routine whatever urgency the GP asks for.

letter:
Dear Cardiologist,

Re: Harold Pemberton, 68

No rush for this one, a routine appointment is fine. Harold has noticed some breathlessness on hills over the past few months, which he puts down to age. In the past three weeks he has twice blacked out briefly while walking uphill to the shops, coming round within a minute with no seizure activity. He has a harsh systolic murmur at the right upper sternal edge. ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy. An echo has been requested.

Kind regards,
Dr Naomi Featherby
note: Syncope on exertion with a murmur suggestive of aortic stenosis is urgent even though the GP asked for routine.
